title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Anor Londo (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : Unlike its Dark Souls counterpart, Anor Londo's illusionary shining sun is gone and has been replaced with the cold blue rays of the moon. The city has noticeably frozen over, as well as being severely reduced in size, with the only remaining parts of the old city being the cathedral, the rotating staircase, and the honorary tomb of Gwyn. An additional tower now stands where the entrance of the building housing the Painted World of Ariamis once stood, with an invisible walkway leading to the top. Additionally, only three of the Silver Knights remain and all Batwing Demons are gone. The cathedral has been overrun by Deacons of the Cathedral of the Deep and Writhing Rotten Flesh. The inside of the cathedral has been covered in corpses and maggots. The eastern section of the cathedral has been blocked off by debris, but the western section is still accessible and contains the body of an old blacksmith.

title: Anor Londo (Dark Souls III)
snippet: In the times of the kingdom of Lothric, things have changed. The beautiful city that once had a glowing sunlight is now cold and dark; the cathedral where the Chosen Undead once fought Ornstein and Smough is now corrupted by the Deep and the home to Gwyndolin, who took his father's title of King of the Gods but fell ill; and the chamber that once held Gwynevere now has nothing but the Sun Princess Ring. A denizen that came from the Painted World, Sulyvahn, infiltrated the city of Irithyll and Gwyndolin's Covenant and later proclaimed himself Pontiff. When Gwyndolin fell ill and became incapable of leading the city and the Covenant, he was forced to retire in the cathedral. The leadership passed to Captain Yorshka, Gwyndolin's crossbreed sister, who was immediately imprisoned by Sulyvahn. Sulyvahn converted Irithyll's knights to the worship of the Deep. The Pontiff then led his master and Saint of the Deep, Aldrich, to devour the helpless Gwyndolin.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet: After Aldrich linked the Flame, a cult formed around his figure, but the deacons of the cathedral also found themselves fighting abominations that emerged from the Deep. The Cathedral, once a peaceful and sacred place for purification, was corrupted by the foul Aldrich, as darkness stagnated and accumulated in the Deep until it had become the final rest of abhorrent creatures. McDonnell found delight in the stagnation of darkness and abandoned his faith in the First Flame and in the gods, devoting himself to the Deep. He spread his belief among the clerics of the cathedral; he even created staffs that channeled faith to produce Deep sorceries, a sacrilegious act. In time the cathedral's deacons became both clergymen and sorcerers, embracing the cult of the Deep and the worship of its Saint, Aldrich.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
Archdeacon McDonnell -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : McDonnell, along with Archdeacons Royce and Klimt, was an archdeacon of the Way of White. The three men managed the Cathedral of the Deep, overseeing its rituals of purification from stagnant Darkness.

At one point, the cathedral welcomed Aldrich, an exiled Irithyllian priest who derived pleasure from eating humans. Aldrich shared his perverse behaviour with others in the cathedral, and sacrifices were brought to him to appease his hunger and grant him the strength to link the First Flame and become a Lord of Cinder.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
Archdeacon McDonnell -  Dark Souls III - character - location 
 location : Archdeacon McDonnell's remains can be found in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, at the Water Reserve.

From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed onward until reaching the building at the end of the big courtyard with several dead Giant Slaves. Upon entering, hit the left wall to uncover an illusory wall. Descend the ladder and dispose of the two Sulyvahn's Beasts waiting at the bottom. Archdeacon McDonnell's remains are located at the far-left corner of the hall, near the Water Reserve bonfire, which will appear once both beasts have been defeated.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet: At some point McDonnell was incapacitated and his body ended up in the lower levels of Irithyll, in a cistern guarded by two of Pontiff Sulyvahn's beasts, however he is still able to recognize others, as he manages Aldrich's covenant and teaches sorceries.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
Archdeacon McDonnell -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : Archdeacon McDonnell, a sorcerer himself, delighted in the cathedral's stagnating souls. For him, they represented the glorious bedrock of this world.

title: Archdeacon McDonnell
snippet:
When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

Once Aldrich defeated Sulyvahn and took control of the city, McDonnell remained to watch over the old Cathedral where the saint was busy digesting Gwyndolin, establishing the covenant of Aldrich Faithful, passing on his dark sorceries to followers who brought him evidence of success in their task.

He was able to obtain said title due to his expert swordsmanship. Eventually, due to the decaying state of the kingdom, he attempted to escape Lothric Castle, though he did not succeed. He wears the Black Hand Set, and wields the Gotthard Twinswords and a Composite Bow.

title: Cathedral Knight
snippet:
A variant of the mace-wielding knight that carries a crossbow can be encountered on the rafters. It will continually snipe at the player with the crossbow until they reach melee range, at which point it will switch to the mace.

The ultra greatsword-wielding variant is considerably more deadly, as on top of being far more aggressive their weapon has a longer reach and deals much more damage. They have a wide variety of horizontal swings, so good dodging is necessary to avoid them. They also possess a kick attack, which is capable of dealing significant damage while knocking the player down a considerable distance. Getting behind them in between their swings can allow the player to land backstabs relatively easily.

title: Cathedral Knight
snippet:
Cathedral Knight -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : The knights wielding maces are capable of buffing their weapon with a variant of Blessed Weapon, which creates small orbs of light that will explode after a short delay. They can also cast Perseverance to greatly improve their defensive power, becoming considerably more aggressive in the process. When they get low on health and are not being immediately attacked, they can pause to cast a healing spell to recover health and buff themselves with a slow heal over time. The Blessed Weapon buff and heal leave them exposed for a few seconds, and it is possible to stagger them out of it, as well as remove the buffs with a Duel Charm.

They will also occasionally attempt to shield bash the player with their greatshields, which they usually perform if they approach the player with their shield up. However, they can also be caught with guard breaks when pacing side-to-side with their shield up, leading to easy ripostes.

title: Cathedral of the Deep
snippet:
Cathedral of the Deep -  Dark Souls III - location - lore 
 lore : The Cathedral of the Deep, as a structure and organization, was founded back in the period in which the Main God of the Way of White was Lloyd. The Cathedral was created with the function of purifying Humans who had their the blood infected by stagnant Dark, a ritual that took place in the Cleansing Chapel in which clerics used notched whips to tear people's flesh and make infected blood flow, to allow the drips to be cleansed. The blood purification process was so effective because the Cathedral was built near the "Deep", a peaceful and sacred place, and therefore infused with the power capable of cleansing the Dark. Due to the rarity of such natural power, the Cathedral was entrusted to at least one Archbishop, the highest rankof the Way of White and direct representative of the Gods.

title: Cathedral of the Deep
snippet:
Cathedral of the Deep -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : The Cathedral of the Deep is the original resting place of Aldrich, Devourer of Gods. His followers, the Deacons, are devoted to sealing away the horrors of The Deep, and the Cathedral owes its existence to this goal. Evangelists were sent to the Undead Settlement from here to spread their message to its inhabitants, and to retrieve Undead as sacrifices.

The path leading up to the Cathedral arrives at the Cleansing Chapel, in which you can find the Notched Whip. The Cleansing Chapel is a hub, reachable from many points within the Cathedral. In this chapel, purification rituals were performed, evidently on the subjects retrieved from the Undead Settlement.

title: Cathedral of the Deep
snippet:
From the plateau, there is an elevator leading to the main gate and a stairway to the second level. This can provide access to Rosaria's Bed Chamber via a moveable bridge. However, another path, leading over the Cathedral's higher balconies and over the rafters, can be accessed by taking a lift close to the Cleansing Chapel. This lift can be reached through a path on the left side of the main hall.

In front of Rosaria's Bed Chamber are numerous Man-grubs which will attack you, but one of them will remain passive. Killing it yields the Red Sign Soapstone. Inside the chamber you will find Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth, and possibly Ringfinger Leonhard depending on your actions.

title: Cathedral of the Deep
snippet:
The Cathedral is surrounded by an immense graveyard where Reanimated Corpses and Infested Corpses rise continuously from their graves. The Grave Wardens are tasked with keeping them under control. The graveyard leads to the Cathedral's front gate, but it is closed. An adjacent path leads across the rooftops, through which you can reach a side entrance. An elevator back to the Cleansing Chapel is close by.

Inside the Cathedral's enormous main hall are two Giant Slaves, each sitting amid a pool of sludge that hinders movement. One is surrounded by numerous pieces of Writhing Rotten Flesh, which can greatly impede you while trying to fight the giant. It guards a stairway to a raised plateau with an altar to Aldrich, with several enemies apparently worshiping here. Beyond the altar is the room containing Aldrich's coffin, guarded by the Deacons of the Deep. For this battle, you may have the choice to summon a variety of friendly phantoms.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Cleric (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Cleric** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Faith-focused class, with decent Attunement, Strength, and Luck. This makes them well-suited to a Miracle-heavy build, and to using the many Lightning-attuned weapons as they are often also have good Strength-scaling.

While it does indeed have spells, in the form of Heal (which heals) and Force (which throws enemies away from you), it does not have any that causes damage, with the earliest ones not being found until Cathedral of the Deep or Farron Keep. This means the class will have to focus primarily on weapons initially, and will do well to keep them upgraded as offensive Miracles consume a lot of Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Cleric (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This is the only spellcasting-focused starting class in Dark Souls 3 that doesn't have a damage-boosting ring. Presumably this is because the Cleric doesn't have a damaging Miracle equipped from the start, and the Morne's Ring can instead be found in the Road of Sacrifices.
This class has remained remarkably similar throughout the series, always carrying a Mace and the Heal Miracle.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet: The Cleric's Sacred Chime is a fairly good casting tool and is actually the strongest casting tool for Miracles from 45 to 49 Faith. Its Spell Buff (the stat that affects how strong scaling spells are) doesn't actually increase until at least 19 Faith has been reached. Its Weapon Art is Gentle Prayer, a regenerative effect that always restores 360 hp over the course of a minute as long as the Chime is held in an active hand (so replacing it with another item stops it, as does two-handing the item in the other hand). This effect will actually outheal the Heal Miracle by up to 20% until the Chime's Spell Buff reaches 120, and even afterwards it is a strong if slow alternative due to only having about a third the cost in Focus Points.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Cleric Set is a light, caster-type armor set and as such has low physical defences and high elemental defences, while also having high Poison and Curse resistances.

The first trainer for more Miracles is found in the Undead Settlement for further development.

title: Cleric (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
The Mace is an unexpectedly strong weapon for what may at first seem like a spellcasting class, but in reality it is often a **Cleric's** main armament. This is because Strike damage is often the strongest physical damage type as armored and skeletal enemies are weak to it (most other physical damage types have fewer enemies weak to them), strong Strength-scaling for easy damage increases, a fairly good moveset, and has a good Weapon Art for trading hits with opponents. How the Weapon Art works is that Perseverance adds a flat 45% extra absorption and causes the attacks of light weapons to bounce off the user, while also granting great Hyper Armor to prevent being staggered.

The Blue Wooden Shield is not very good, having only decent physical and magic defence with serviceable Stability. While it does have Parry (albeit the inferior Medium Shield version), a strong Weapon Skill shield like the early Silver Eagle Kite Shield would probably serve as a better replacement.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet:
Company Captain Yorshka -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Yorshka is the younger sister of Dark Sun Gwyndolin, with whom she shares only her mother, as her brother is Gwyn's lastborn. She claims to have little knowledge of the world, to the point of only knowing crows and dragons as beings capable of flight, implying that she was raised in isolation, perhaps in the Painted World of Ariamis. Furthermore, as of arriving at Irithyll, the girl didn't even have a name.

She is voiced by Martha Mackintosh.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet: Amidst the power vacuum left by Gwyndolin's absence, Sulyvahn would take advantage of the fragile situation, declaring himself Pontiff and becoming the tyrant of Irithyll. He managed to imprison Yorshka on the tower of her own church, isolating her from the world and holding her hostage. Over time, the Darkmoon would lose every one of its followers, being integrated into the ranks of Sulyvahn's knights, killed, or exiled, leaving Yorshka as the head of a covenant with no knights and only its legacy to preserve. Yorshka would have remained alone on the tower, unable to hear from her brother, with only the chime that he had given her to console her in her solitude. Despite her imprisonment, the humans of Irithyll, now enslaved by Pontiff Sulyvahn and subjected to his experiments, would continue to pray to the goddess in secret, worshipping the sacred spears that were enchanted with a soporific spell, trying to find comfort and rest from their condition, even at the cost of hitting

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet:
Company Captain Yorshka -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : Yorshka's outfit, described as a Saint's set, is available for the player to wear in removed content. According to the item description, Yorshka was originally imprisoned in a dungeon (the tower where she is found, according to dialogue after advancing her covenant to level 2 or higher) and her outfit, originally pure white, was stained ash grey from years of incarceration.
Another article of removed content, Gwyndolin's Finger, could be presumably obtained upon defeating Aldrich. It could be given to Yorshka for additional dialogue and a reward, presumably Darkmoon Ring based on the dialogue. According to its item description, she is a crossbreed.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet:
Company Captain Yorshka -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : Captain Yorshka is the leader of the Darkmoon Blades and accepts the player into their ranks if they have learned the Darkmoon Loyalty gesture.

She is a tall and slim woman, with pale skin, blue eyes with scale-like markings around them, and dark green hair. She also has two pairs of pointy ears, with the larger pair having long and rigid lobes, as well as two long lobe-like tentacles hanging from her upper neck. She wears a white dress and a veil over her hair. She is barefoot and appears to have a tail not unlike that of a dragon. Yorshka talks in an older form of English, and lives in a tower secluded from the rest of Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet:
Company Captain Yorshka -  Dark Souls III - character - theories 
 theories : One theory is that Yorshka comes from the Painted World of Ariamis.
**She comes from such an isolated place that she only knows about dragons and crows as flying creatures. It is noteworthy that crows and dragons were presumably the only aerial creatures in that Painted World.
**The Painting Guardian Set can be found in her church, which was built in the same location where the Painted World was kept in ancient Anor Londo.
**Her appearance, given her likely origins in the Painted World, make it highly plausible that she has some relation to Crossbreed Priscilla, the only woman known to possess draconic traits within the Painted World. In addition, she bore no name just like the other daughter of Priscilla, until Gwyndolin gifted her with one.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet:
Company Captain Yorshka -  Dark Souls III - character - location 
 location : She is located in Anor Londo, dwelling alone atop the Prison Tower that rises high above the Church of Yorshka. It can be accessed from the rotating elevator located after the Darkmoon Tomb in Anor Londo. The tower can be reached regardless of the position of the elevator. The tower is visible in the distance and requires a step of faith onto open air to reveal an invisible bridge that leads to it.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet: After Gwyndolin was "stricken by illness" and forced to retreat to the old cathedral of Anor Londo, her brother entrusted Yorshka with command of the covenant of the Blades of the Darkmoon. The girl thus assumed leadership the company, reciting her brother's ritual phrases by heart; and guided its knights' vigil over those who would link the First Flame, with the Blades shielding them from those who would oppose the will of the Gods. Per tradition, Yorshka continued to accept proofs of the knights' accomplished duty and rewarded them with the miracles of Gwyndolin, herself ignorant of their vengeful connotations.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet: At some point, after Gwyndolin had become the "Chief Deity" of the Anor Londo clan, Yorshka reached Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, the city her brother had built on the ruins of Anor Londo to house the Irithyllians, hybrids between the race of the gods of Anor Londo and humans. Here she was welcomed by Gwyndolin who formed a relationship of deep affection with his newfound sister, giving her a sacred chime and even the name Yorshka. Eventually a church was built in her name inside Irithyll—exactly where the Painted World of Ariamis was once kept— in which she was venerated as a goddess by the humans who worked in the city.

title: Corvian
snippet:
Corvian -  Dark Souls III - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Corvians are almost completely vulnerable before starting their transformation. However, if they have already started it and are attacked, the transformation will complete immediately, rendering them able to retaliate. They stagger easily, though, and fast weapons like straight swords should leave them with no opportunity to counterattack. If a heavy weapon is used, the player should make sure that the corvian will die in one or two hits.

It is not advisable to engage more than one of these creatures at a time due to the constant damage output they can deal and their quick recovery times. If they are found congregated in front of a storyteller, either the latter should be dealt first or each corvian should be drawn in individually with ranged attacks. In some cases, if the storyteller dies, all remaining corvians will become completely oblivious to the player, making for easy kills.

title: Slumbering Dragoncrest Ring (Dark Souls II)
snippet:

title: Target Shield (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Target Shield (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Target Shield has relatively low requirements to wield, though unlike most other shields it requires at least a small amount of investment in Dexterity. Like other Small Shields, it does not provide very much protection when used to block attacks.

What sets the Target Shield apart from its peers is that it is one of three Parrying Shields in the game, along with the Small Leather Shield and the Buckler, with active parrying frames starting up faster than on most other Small Shields. In this regard, the Target Shield provides the best of both worlds, possessing a higher stability and physical absorption than the other two Parrying Shields, which allows it to somewhat safeguard its wielder from attacks.

snippet:
Karla -  Dark Souls III - character - location 
 location : Karla is located in a locked cell in the lower level of the Irithyll Dungeon, in the area with numerous Jailers. In order to unlock it, the player must have the Jailer's Key Ring, found in the Profaned Capital, and then go back to the Irithyll Dungeon once more to free her.

After exhausting her dialogue and agreeing to rescue her, Karla will relocate to Firelink Shrine and become a merchant there. She can be found under the stairs to the left of Andre's smithy. Unlike most Firelink Shrine characters, she has no questline, nor does she relocate after all of her wares have been purchased, and will remain in Firelink Shrine regardless of the player's actions unless killed.

title: Broadsword (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Broadsword (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - availability 
 availability : Found in the High Wall of Lothric, beyond the Tower on the Wall bonfire, in the room where Greirat's cell key is found. The corpse holding it is found in a small room in which a longsword-wielding hollow is found guarding it.

title: Throwing Knife (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Throwing Knife (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - item - description 
 description : Throwing knife. Used as a projectile.

This simple weapon does not require much in the way of practice to use. However, it does not deal much in the way of damage either. Regardless, it is still a valuable tool to have by one's side in the absence of other ranged attack options.

title: Old Ironclad Armor
snippet:
Old Ironclad Armor -  Dark Souls II - armor - trivia 
 trivia : Although not mentioned in the in-game description, it does in fact stop backstabs.

title: Prowling Magus
snippet:
Prowling Magus -  Dark Souls II - enemy - notes 
 notes : The Magus encountered in the original game does not respawn.
The Magus encountered in *Scholar of the First Sin* does respawn.

title: Manikin Shield
snippet:
Manikin Shield -  Dark Souls II - shield - description 
 description : The Manikin Shield has fairly high physical damage reduction for a small shield, but quite low elemental resistances. The shield does, however, have above average Poison, Bleed, Petrification and Curse reduction in relation to its light weight, making it a good choice for characters with low Vitality in areas where negative status effects are common.

title: Stone Greatsword
snippet:
Stone Greatsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - trivia 
 trivia : When the Stone Knights use this weapon, it does not do Magic damage like it does when the player uses it.

title: Astora Straight Sword
snippet:
Astora Straight Sword -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Although it has a minimum requirement in Faith in order to be used effectively, the Astora Straight Sword does not scale with Faith (unless it is infused down the Blessed/Lightning path), nor is it innately-blessed (unlike Anri's Straight Sword).

While it does have higher base damage than the Long Sword, it should be noted that it scales worse in Dexterity, and continues to scale unremarkably with both Strength and Dexterity, even at maximum reinforcement, and when it is made into a refined weapon.

Unlike its *Dark Souls* variant, it does not have magic damage or blessed damage.

title: Way of White
snippet:
Way of White -  Dark Souls - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Players may join the Way of White by talking either to Petrus at the Firelink Shrine or Reah after you have rescued her from the Tomb of the Giants.

Players who choose to be in the Knight class or the Cleric class begin the game already in the Way of White. (Though this does not unlock the trophy/achievement for discovering the Way of White covenant. Unlocking the trophy/achievement as a knight or cleric will require abandoning the covenant and then re-joining via talking to Petrus or Reah).

title: Carthus of the Sands
snippet:
Carthus of the Sands -  Dark Souls III - location - lead 
 lead : is a mentioned location in *Dark Souls III*. What the player passes through are only the catacombs of the ancient kingdom.

title: Antiquated Key
snippet:
Antiquated Key -  Dark Souls II - shield - description 
 description : This key is very old, but in very good condition, such that it should still function.

Only, what lock does this key fit?

title: Emit Force (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Emit Force (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - spell - availability 
 availability : Obtained as a gift from Siegward of Catarina by exhausting his dialogue in the kitchen found after the sewer area in Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

title: Rusted Coin (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Rusted Coin (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - item - notes 
 notes : Effect stacks with other items that boosts Item Discovery.
Using this coin along with the Symbol of Avarice, the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring +3, and the Crystal Sage's Rapier will increase Item Discovery up to 315 units.
Can be used on ladders.
Copper does not rust, though it does oxidize, becoming green or bluish green. This is very likely what is covering most of the coin.

title: Rubbish (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Rubbish (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - item - notes 
 notes : Unlike in previous *Souls* games where these items could be sometimes traded in exchange for better ones, in *Dark Souls III* they have absolutely no use and are best discarded as soon as they are obtained.
**Receiving only one soul for each of them if sold, it isn't even worth the bother of hanging on to them.
**A more unorthodox use for Rubbish is leaving it on the ground during an invasion to lure unsuspecting players (as players won't know what the item is until picked up).

title: Peculiar Doll
snippet:
Peculiar Doll -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : The Peculiar Doll is used to enter the Painted World of Ariamis. To enter the Painted World, players need to have the Peculiar Doll in their inventory and examine the large painting in the cathedral in Anor Londo.

The Peculiar doll is lost at the end of each playthrough and must be collected again in order to access the Painted World in NG+.

title: Thief Mask (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Thief Mask (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - armor - trivia 
 trivia : Unlike previous iterations, the female version of the Thief Mask in *Dark Souls III* does not remove the hood from the wearer's head.

title: Red Hilted Halberd
snippet:
Red Hilted Halberd -  Dark Souls III - weapon - availability 
 availability : Found in the Undead Settlement's sewers. The Grave Key is required to unlock the gate in the sewage system that gives access to this area. It is found at the center of the room where the player is attacked by Skeletons for the first time.

title: Black Knight Set (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Black Knight Set (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Black Knight Set offers overall mediocre physical defenses for its weight. What it does have is decent Poise and very high Flame Defense, which ranks as the highest of any medium set when fully upgraded.

title: Lost Sinner
snippet:
Lost Sinner -  Dark Souls II - boss - trivia 
 trivia : The original Japanese term used for "sinner" (罪人) does not possess any gender meaning to it, being instead neutral.
In the JP text Sweet Shalquoir says that she tried to create (生みだ) the First Flame rather than light it, which is more equivalent to what the Witch of Izalith tried to do.

title: Executioner's Chariot
snippet: Phase two begins when the chariot bashes into the gate. The horse will be free as the chariot is completely destroyed and the charioteer is killed. The horse is very easy to fight and behaves similarly as the Fang Boar from the first *Dark Souls*. The horse has a charge attack where it bashes you with its head, this move is unblockable and does damage through your shield. If you linger behind the horse for too long, it will kick at you with its hind legs. If you are in front of it for too long, it will stand up on its hind legs and bash downwards on you. If you are at a medium distance away, the horse will spew a Dark fog that is unblockable and does heavy damage through your shield.

title: Soul of a Champion
snippet:
Soul of a Champion -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Can only be obtained in NG+ onward, where it replaces the Soul of a Crestfallen Knight.

title: Dragon Greatsword
snippet:
Dragon Greatsword -  Dark Souls - weapon - availability 
 availability : Obtained by cutting off the Stone Dragon's tail in Ash Lake. Doing so does not count as a betrayal to the Path of the Dragon covenant, as the Stone Dragon is invulnerable and will always remain passive. Players will need to deal 459 damage to the tail in order to cut it in the base game cycle.

title: Soul of a Proud Paladin
snippet:
Soul of a Proud Paladin -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Can only be obtained in NG+ onward, where it replaces the Soul of a Deserted Corpse.

title: Soul of a Seasoned Warrior
snippet:
Soul of a Seasoned Warrior -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Can only be obtained in NG+ onward, where it replaces the Soul of a Nameless Soldier.

title: Soul of an Intrepid Hero
snippet:
Soul of an Intrepid Hero -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Can only be obtained in NG+ onward, where it replaces the Soul of an Unknown Traveler.

title: Soul of an Old Hand
snippet:
Soul of an Old Hand -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Can only be obtained in NG+ onward, where it replaces the Soul of a Weary Warrior.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This class is fairly popular amongst speedrunners thanks to Spook making it possible to easier skip foes and falls.
While the Assassin doesn't have any direct equivalent class in the Dark Souls series, it does bear some resemblance to the Royalty class from FromSoftware's previous game Demon's Souls, another Dexterity/Intelligence-based class wielding a thrusting sword (in that case a Rapier) and a small shield while also providing access to a Sorcery-like spell (though in the Royalty's case it is the offensive Soul Arrow, not a self-buffing spell).

title: Wolnir's Crown
snippet:
Wolnir's Crown -  Dark Souls III - armor - notes 
 notes : Contrary to what one would expect from a unique boss armor piece, the crown does not grant any special abilities.

title: Siegward of Catarina
snippet:
Siegward of Catarina -  Dark Souls III - character - jailed_in_irithyll_dungeon 
 jailed_in_irithyll_dungeon : The last place Siegward can be found is in the Irithyll Dungeon, locked in a cell. In order to free him, the player must obtain the Old Cell Key and find the hidden entrance located in Profaned Capital to his cell to unlock it; there is an opening near the Court Sorcerer that can be reached by jumping from the rooftop. Within the cell is the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring. Once Siegward has been freed, he will thank the player and grant them a Titanite Slab as a gift.

title: Rickert of Vinheim
snippet:
Rickert of Vinheim -  Dark Souls - character - strategy 
 strategy : The only way to hurt Rickert is through the use of a long weapon, such as the Titanite Catch Pole or Demon's Spear. While Rickert does not fight back, it is easy to fall off the ledge accidentally. As Rickert can also be hurt by Wrath of the Gods using it is safer since it does not require movement.
